findings.name: "Redirect to HTTPS" setting shows the Site url description text instead of its own
findings.summary: The 'Redirect to HTTPS' toggle shows the Site url text: "This URL is used for things like creating links in emails, auth redirects, and in some embedding scenarios, so changing it could break functionality or get you locked out of this instance." It describes a URL and lockout, which makes no sense for an on/off switch and misleads the admin about what the toggle does. (on /admin/settings/general)
findings.expected: The 'Redirect to HTTPS' toggle should have its own description explaining what redirecting to HTTPS does.
findings.actual: The 'Redirect to HTTPS' toggle shows the Site url text: "This URL is used for things like creating links in emails, auth redirects, and in some embedding scenarios, so changing it could break functionality or get you locked out of this instance." It describes a URL and lockout, which makes no sense for an on/off switch and misleads the admin about what the toggle does.
reproSteps: Sign in with eval@momentic.ai and open /admin/settings/general
Look at the 'App config' card, at the 'Redirect to HTTPS' toggle below 'Site url'
Read the description line under the 'Redirect to HTTPS' heading

findings.name: Site url description paragraph is repeated twice in the same block
findings.summary: The sentence "This URL is used for things like creating links in emails, auth redirects, and in some embedding scenarios, so changing it could break functionality or get you locked out of this instance." appears twice in the Site url block: once right after "Only change this if you know what you're doing!" and again as a separate identical paragraph above the "This has been set by the MB_SITE_URL environment variable." line. (on /admin/settings/general)
findings.expected: The Site url description should appear once.
findings.actual: The sentence "This URL is used for things like creating links in emails, auth redirects, and in some embedding scenarios, so changing it could break functionality or get you locked out of this instance." appears twice in the Site url block: once right after "Only change this if you know what you're doing!" and again as a separate identical paragraph above the "This has been set by the MB_SITE_URL environment variable." line.
reproSteps: Sign in with eval@momentic.ai and open /admin/settings/general
In the 'App config' card, read the whole 'Site url' block, from its heading down to the environment-variable line

findings.name: 'Email address for help requests' saves an invalid address with \"Changes saved\"
findings.summary: The value is saved as soon as the field loses focus: a "Changes saved" toast appears and the field keeps "not-an-email". No validation message, no refused save — the instance's help email is now an invalid address. (on /admin/settings/general)
findings.expected: The page should refuse a value that is not an email address (a validation message next to the field) and keep the previous valid address.
findings.actual: The value is saved as soon as the field loses focus: a "Changes saved" toast appears and the field keeps "not-an-email". No validation message, no refused save — the instance's help email is now an invalid address.
reproSteps: Scroll to the 'Email and tracking' card
Select the text in the 'Email address for help requests' field and type not-an-email
Press Tab to leave the field

findings.name: "Find someone" search treats % and _ as wildcards and lists every person
findings.summary: Typing % lists all 3 people (Harbor Admin, Jordan Ellis, Maya Chen) and says '3 people found'; a single _ does the same. The backend call /api/user?query=%25 passes the text unescaped, so % and _ act as SQL LIKE wildcards instead of literal characters in the filter. (on /admin/people)
findings.expected: A search for % (a character that does not occur in any name or email) finds no people and shows the 'No results found' empty state, as typing 'zzz' already does.
findings.actual: Typing % lists all 3 people (Harbor Admin, Jordan Ellis, Maya Chen) and says '3 people found'; a single _ does the same. The backend call /api/user?query=%25 passes the text unescaped, so % and _ act as SQL LIKE wildcards instead of literal characters in the filter.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval@momentic.ai and open /admin/people.
Wait for the list to update and read the rows and the footer count.
